chapters.before: Respiratory infections and waterborne diarrheal diseases regularly overwhelmed the pediatric ward in Pariang during rainy seasons.
chapters.supported: Raus implemented systematic triage protocols, standardized rehydration therapy, and administered essential antibiotic treatments.
chapters.changed: Pediatric hospital stay durations have shortened, and recovery rates for acute pediatric illnesses now exceed 96%.

support.label: Pediatric Ward Inpatient Care
support.detail: Continuous nursing and diagnostic monitoring

support.label: Oral Rehydration & Antibiotics
support.detail: Timely administration of life-saving medical treatments

name: Rumia Kafi
role: Midwife & Maternal Care Specialist (Nuba Mountains), Pariang
headline: Providing culturally sensitive maternal healthcare to Nuba refugee families and host communities.
quote: No matter how difficult the journey has been, our clinic is a sanctuary of life and healing.

chapters.before: Expectant mothers fleeing aerial bombardments and hunger in the Nuba Mountains arrived in Pariang severely anemic and physically depleted.
chapters.supported: Rumia provides intensive antenatal nutrition support, iron-folate therapy, and dedicated one-on-one midwifery during labor.
chapters.changed: Hundreds of vulnerable mothers have given birth to healthy newborns, finding safety and renewal in Pariang.

support.label: Refugee Maternity Support
support.detail: Compassionate obstetric care tailored to displaced mothers

support.label: Maternal Anemia Treatment
support.detail: Nutritional supplements and prenatal health checks

name: Diana
role: Senior Midwife & Clinical Skills Educator, PHSI Juba
headline: Instructing midwifery students in advanced clinical simulations and emergency obstetrics.
quote: Precision and compassion in the classroom translate into lives saved in rural clinics.

chapters.before: A shortage of practical simulation equipment and instructors in Juba made it difficult for midwifery students to practice emergency procedures before ward placements.
chapters.supported: Diana developed structured mannequin simulation drills covering shoulder dystocia, neonatal resuscitation, and eclampsia management.
chapters.changed: Graduates report feeling thoroughly prepared and confident when facing complex obstetric emergencies in rural state clinics.

support.label: Clinical Simulation Lab
support.detail: Hands-on emergency obstetric procedure training

support.label: Curriculum Standards
support.detail: Aligning midwifery instruction with national health guidelines

name: Maria
headline: Supervising clinical inpatient recovery and hospital nursing standards in Juba.
quote: Continuous vigilance at the patient's bedside makes all the difference in recovery.

chapters.before: High patient turnover in urban clinics often led to rushed post-operative monitoring and delayed recognition of surgical complications.
chapters.supported: Maria instituted strict hourly vital signs monitoring protocols, wound infection audits, and patient-centred nursing care.
chapters.changed: Post-operative complications and hospital readmissions have dropped by over 40% across her ward.

support.label: Inpatient Ward Supervision
support.detail: Overseeing 30-bed surgical and maternal recovery ward

support.label: Clinical Care Audits
support.detail: Maintaining high patient safety and hygiene standards

name: Mary Keji
headline: Coordinating clinical placements and maternal health delivery across Juba.

portrait.alt: Mary Keji, health specialist in Juba

quote: Strong maternal health systems are built on well-trained, respected midwives.

chapters.before: Coordination between training institutes and hospital maternity wards in Central Equatoria was fragmented, leaving clinical students without mentorship.
chapters.supported: Mary Keji oversees student clinical rotations, ensuring every trainee attends a minimum of 50 supervised deliveries before certification.
chapters.changed: A steady pipeline of certified, highly competent midwives enters the workforce each year, ready for immediate field deployment.

support.label: Clinical Rotation Oversight
support.detail: Coordinating hospital practicals for PHSI students

support.label: Quality Maternal Assurance
support.detail: Reviewing delivery standards across partner health centres

name: Alok
headline: Promoting institutional deliveries and safe motherhood across Western Bahr el Ghazal.
quote: When women feel respected and heard in the maternity ward, they encourage their sisters to deliver safely.

chapters.before: Rural mothers around Wau frequently opted for risky home deliveries because of fear of unfamiliar medical environments and language barriers.
chapters.supported: Alok introduced respectful maternity care standards, free clean delivery packs, and antenatal health talks in local languages.
chapters.changed: More than 80% of pregnant women in her target payams now choose facility delivery, with dramatic reductions in newborn infections.

support.label: Respectful Maternity Ward
support.detail: Culturally sensitive care and birth companion support

support.label: Clean Delivery Kits
support.detail: Supplying expectant mothers with sterile delivery essentials

name: Teresa
role: Midwife & Emergency Maternal Lead, Abyei / Agok
headline: Delivering frontline obstetric care in conflict-affected border communities in Abyei.
quote: Even when insecurity shakes our border communities, the arrival of new life brings unshakeable hope.

chapters.before: Recurring cross-border skirmishes and displacement in the Abyei corridor left pregnant women cut off from reliable surgical and delivery facilities.
chapters.supported: Teresa established an emergency obstetric triage tent in Agok/Abyei with solar-powered lights, sterile surgical packs, and maternal rehydration.
chapters.changed: Mothers displaced by fighting find a safe, welcoming clinic where skilled midwives stand ready at any hour.

support.label: Emergency Border Delivery Post
support.detail: Rapid maternal care during displacement

support.label: Sterile Instrument Supplies
support.detail: Life-saving tools for complicated deliveries

name: Teresa
role: Community Midwife, Koch County Health Care Centre
headline: Delivering skilled care in flood-affected and remote villages across Koch County.
quote: Water surrounding our village cannot stop us from protecting our mothers.

chapters.before: Severely damaged infrastructure in Koch County left most pregnant women without access to trained midwives during labor.
chapters.supported: Teresa rehabilitated the local health centre's delivery room, equipped it with clean linens and birth kits, and conducts weekly mobile visits.
chapters.changed: Mothers who previously gave birth without assistance now deliver safely with Teresa, knowing their newborns are protected.

support.label: Rehabilitated Delivery Room
support.detail: Dry, sterile birth room in Koch PHCC

support.label: Weekly Mobile Clinic
support.detail: Reaching isolated homesteads across Koch

name: Nyawal
role: Midwife & Maternal Outreach Specialist, Ayod County
headline: Navigating vast wetlands to bring safe delivery care to mothers across Ayod.
quote: Every village in Ayod deserves access to trained hands when new life enters the world.

chapters.before: Deep floods created islands across Ayod County, preventing women from walking to health facilities and leaving them vulnerable to birth trauma.
chapters.supported: Nyawal established a community canoe-based referral system, training village birth attendants to alert her when labor starts.
chapters.changed: Mothers in the most remote payams are now safely transported or attended to by Nyawal, eliminating delays in maternal care.

support.label: Canoe Maternal Referral System
support.detail: Waterborne transport for mothers in labor

support.label: Village Attendant Mentorship
support.detail: Training local women in safe birth practices

name: Elizabeth
headline: Restoring maternal health services in flood-hit communities of Mayendit County.
quote: Seeing healthy mothers and crying babies brings light back to our community in Mayendit.

chapters.before: Floods submerged farmland and homes in Mayendit, forcing mothers to give birth in damp, unsanitary conditions with high infant infection rates.
chapters.supported: Elizabeth set up an elevated, dry maternity shelter equipped with solar power, clean birth kits, and newborn warmth packs.
chapters.changed: Expectant mothers have a safe haven for labor and delivery, and infant sepsis has been virtually eradicated in the catchment area.

support.label: Elevated Maternity Shelter
support.detail: Flood-proof delivery facility in Mayendit

support.detail: Sterile cord care, warm blankets, and caps

name: Nyachudier
headline: Carrying forward the proud heritage of PRDA's Leer Midwifery Training School.
quote: The Leer Midwifery School taught us that our hands hold the future of South Sudan.

chapters.before: Leer was once the historic centre of PRDA's midwifery training before conflicts disrupted classrooms and displaced students across regions.
chapters.supported: Having graduated from the accredited midwifery programme, Nyachudier returned to Leer to serve in the community clinic, attending births and mentoring apprentices.
chapters.changed: The tradition of skilled midwifery in Leer is alive and strong, with hundreds of women receiving life-saving care every month.

support.detail: Full obstetric and neonatal care in Leer

name: Gatwech
role: Emergency Relief & Community WASH Lead, Canal/Pigi
headline: Coordinating emergency flood assistance and canal-side community dialogues in Canal/Pigi.
quote: When floodwaters rise along the canal, rapid assistance and unity between our communities save lives.

chapters.before: Seasonal overflowing of the White Nile and Jonglei Canal submerged farmland and cut off access to potable water across Canal/Pigi, triggering clan displacement and resource tensions.
chapters.supported: Through PRDA's emergency response and peacebuilding teams, Gatwech distributed clean water purification kits, rehabilitated hand pumps on higher ground, and facilitated water-sharing councils.
chapters.changed: Displaced families have access to safe drinking water and emergency shelter supplies, while community peace monitors prevent resource clashes during high water.

support.label: Canal-Side WASH Response
support.detail: Borehole repair and water purification supplies

name: Chuol
headline: Mediating cattle migration pacts and healing clan trauma across Ayod County.
quote: True peace takes root when youth trade weapons for dialogue and shared trade.

chapters.before: Cattle raids and historical boundary disputes in the Ayod wetlands repeatedly forced youth into cycles of retaliatory violence that disrupted village life.
chapters.supported: Under PRDA's Peace Building and Conflict Transformation initiative, Chuol established joint youth and elder peace councils and negotiated agreed dry-season grazing corridors.
chapters.changed: Cattle migrations across payams now proceed peacefully under joint monitoring committees, and inter-clan markets have reopened without fear.

support.label: Wetland Dialogue Councils
support.detail: Facilitating inter-payam mediation forums in Ayod

support.label: Youth Peace Monitor Training
support.detail: Equipping 40 cattle camp youth in conflict de-escalation

name: Rev. James
role: Faith-Based Peacebuilding & National Dialogue Coordinator, Juba
headline: Convening church leaders, traditional chiefs, and youth for national reconciliation.

portrait.alt: Rev. James, peacebuilding coordinator in Juba

quote: When the church and traditional leaders speak with one voice for peace, communities find the courage to forgive and unite.

chapters.before: National and regional political fissures in South Sudan frequently fractured community cohesion along ethnic and denominational lines.
chapters.supported: Rev. James coordinates high-level faith forums and grassroots trauma-healing workshops from PRDA's Juba headquarters, bringing divided leaders to one table.
chapters.changed: Faith leaders across the Upper Nile and Equatoria corridors now maintain a unified reconciliation council that acts rapidly to mediate local escalations.

name: Dr. Taban
role: Mobile Medical Camps Lead & Clinical Officer, Juba
headline: Organizing free community medical camps and mobile clinical checkups across Juba.

quote: A medical camp brings high-standard clinical care right to families who cannot afford hospital transport or prescription fees.

chapters.before: Families in peri-urban settlements and displacement sites around Juba (such as Gondokoro and Northern Bari) faced severe economic hurdles to access basic diagnostic care.
chapters.supported: Dr. Taban mobilizes volunteer doctors, PHSI nurses, and pharmacy kits to set up free weekend medical camps offering general consultations, malaria tests, and hypertension care.
chapters.changed: Thousands of vulnerable residents receive immediate diagnosis, free essential medicines, and urgent surgical referrals without financial barrier.

name: Gatkuoth
headline: Facilitating grassroots peace dialogues and restorative justice across Leer County.
quote: Healing the wounds of conflict in Leer begins when neighbours sit together under the shade of the dialogue tree.

chapters.before: Protracted conflict and clan divisions in southern Unity State left deep mistrust, cutting off trade between payams and keeping cattle camp youth armed and anxious.
chapters.supported: Through PRDA's Peace Building and Conflict Transformation initiative, Gatkuoth facilitated community-led peace pacts, trauma-informed mediation sessions, and joint youth peace forums.
chapters.changed: Cattle grazing corridors and fishing waters are now shared peacefully between payams, and inter-clan disputes are resolved through mediation rather than violence.

name: Nyanuer
role: WASH Supervisor & Water Committee Lead, Leer
headline: Restoring community water boreholes and training hygiene promoters across flood-prone Leer.

portrait.alt: Nyanuer at a borehole in Leer

quote: When clean water flows right in our village, our daughters attend school and our children stay healthy.

chapters.before: Severe flooding submerged community boreholes across Leer, contaminating water tables and leading to recurring surges of acute watery diarrhea among young children.
chapters.supported: Through the ACT Alliance flood response, Nyanuer led the rehabilitation of elevated hand pumps, decontaminated deep wells, and trained women-led water management committees.
chapters.changed: Clean, reliable drinking water is protected against floodwaters, and women caretakers manage spare parts and monthly upkeep independently.

name: Deng
role: Emergency Relief & Flood Response Coordinator, Leer
headline: Coordinating rapid emergency shelter and non-food relief for flood-displaced families in Leer.
quote: When floodwaters rise in the night, getting dry shelter and food kits into families' hands gives them dignity and survival.

chapters.before: Seasonal dike breaches left hundreds of families homeless overnight, stranded on small mounds of high ground with no blankets, cooking pots, or waterproof shelter.
chapters.supported: Deng mobilizes rapid response teams under PRDA and ACT Alliance appeal SSD241, distributing emergency tarpaulins, mosquito nets, hygiene packs, and cash-for-work dike repair assistance.
chapters.changed: Displaced families receive emergency shelter and household essentials within 48 hours of flood displacement, and reinforced dikes protect homesteads.

name: Veronica Nyakuoth
role: Midwife, Ulang Primary Health Care Centre
headline: Delivering skilled maternal and newborn care along the Sobat River corridor in Ulang.
quote: Every mother arriving on the riverbanks deserves compassionate, skilled care when giving birth.

chapters.before: During seasonal rains, high waters cut off overland access to Ulang hospital, leaving mothers in outer villages with only unassisted home deliveries.
chapters.supported: Veronica established a 24-hour maternal health post at Ulang PHCC, equipped with sterile delivery packs, maternal rehydration, and infant warming.
chapters.changed: Mothers now travel early by canoe to stay near the clinic before delivery, and complication rates have dropped drastically across the county.

support.detail: 24/7 skilled labor and delivery attendance

name: Nyakor
role: Midwife, Mandeang Primary Health Care Unit
headline: Providing skilled delivery and antenatal care in Mandeang payam, Nasir County.
quote: Serving mothers here in Mandeang means bringing life and safety to one of our most remote communities.

chapters.before: Mandeang payam had no resident certified midwife for years, forcing families to undertake arduous boat journeys to Nasir town during obstructed labor.
chapters.supported: Deployed with PRDA's PHSI support, Nyakor opened the maternity room at Mandeang PHCU, providing prenatal testing, malaria treatment, and safe deliveries.
chapters.changed: Mothers throughout Mandeang and neighbouring river hamlets now deliver locally with skilled medical hands by their side.

support.detail: Skilled obstetric care and sterile supplies
